Assertions.Description: Enable Workspaces and use Settings Launch editor: exactly one Workspaces Editor opens with the workspace list.
The real Quick Access Workspaces entry opens the same Workspaces Editor window.
With the editor closed, the exact default chord displayed in Settings opens Workspaces Editor.
Save an unused activation chord and confirm the new physical chord opens the editor.
The previous physical chord no longer opens the editor; restore the original afterward.
Disable Workspaces and confirm Settings Launch editor is disabled.
The activation chord does not open the disabled editor.
Quick Access has no usable disabled-module launch action.
Command Palette retains Workspaces settings but not Open Workspaces editor or per-workspace results.
Re-enable and verify Settings, Quick Access, configured chord and Command Palette results work without restarting Windows.
Clean install/profile without settings.json: Workspaces is disabled from first render and never starts/enables transiently before defaults persist.
Capture includes every prepared app once, including the restored fixture opened after Snapshot Creator started waiting.
Both restored apps expose matching recorded non-zero Left, Top, Width and Height.
The packaged maximized app, minimized app and preview reflect their captured states.
Save a unique name: exactly one matching card appears with the correct app count and all icons/previews.
Non-elevated PowerToys capture omits the elevated fixture.
Elevated PowerToys capture includes that fixture with Launch as administrator checked.
Cancel Snapshot Creator returns to the list without changing the recorded workspace count or persisted data.
On two differently scaled monitors, each capture overlay exactly covers its monitor without offset, gap, overlap or spill.
A unique workspace-name substring leaves only the matching card.
An application name present in only one of two distinct workspaces leaves only that card.
Clearing Search restores the full list.
Known launch history sorts Last launched newest-first.
Known creation order sorts Created newest-first.
Known names sort Name alphabetically ascending.
After closing every owned editor and reopening, non-default selection and card order persist.
More > Remove immediately removes the selected card without confirmation.
Only that record is removed from Workspaces data; other workspaces remain.
More > Edit opens the selected workspace with its correct name and applications.
Clicking another card body, not Launch or More, edits that card's workspace.
At wide and narrow editor sizes, cards stretch and Launch/More remain reachable.
With enough workspaces to scroll, vertical scrolling neither clips content nor creates an unusable nested horizontal scroll area.
Removing one of at least two apps moves it to removed state and removes its preview while the other remains unchanged.
Add back restores the removed app's original monitor group, preview position and saved launch properties.
Set a restored app to Minimized: position fields and preview update appropriately.
Set another restored app to Maximized: position fields and preview update appropriately.
Save and reopen: both states persist.
For an admin-capable Win32 fixture, save Launch as administrator on, launch and approve UAC: process is elevated and arranged.
Turn it off, save and relaunch: process is non-elevated and arranged.
Win32 command-line arguments targeting a unique file/folder persist after saving and reopening.
Workspace launch passes those arguments to the correct process and opens that target.
Known non-zero Custom Left, Top, Width and Height update the preview immediately.
Save, close and reopen: the custom values persist, not 0,0.
The launched real window matches the saved rectangle within recorded normal frame tolerance.
Save a unique rename and app-property change: return to the list, then reopen and verify both values.
The card and existing desktop shortcut use the new name; the obsolete shortcut name is removed.
Change a name/app property and Cancel: return to the list and reopen with the original value.
After an unsaved change, Workspaces breadcrumb returns to the list without persisting it.
Check Create desktop shortcut and save: the named .lnk appears and the reopened checkbox is checked.
With fixture apps closed, invoking .lnk launches the same app set and placement as editor Launch.
Delete the test shortcut and reopen: the checkbox is unchecked.
Launch and edit a scrollable workspace, wait for its apps, open an additional fixture and Capture: additional app included and existing apps represented once each.
Wide/narrow editing views keep Save, Cancel, preview, project properties and expanded app controls reachable without horizontal clipping.
Save Move existing windows enabled, leave a matching app at wrong coordinates, launch: that exact window moves to the saved rectangle.
Save Move existing windows disabled, leave a matching app at wrong coordinates, launch: that exact window remains in place.
Close the isolated Win32 app then Launch: correct executable starts exactly once and moves to its saved state/monitor.
Close the packaged app then Launch: correct package starts exactly once and moves to its saved state/monitor.
Launcher lists every configured valid and intentionally invalid app.
Each row transitions through the appropriate launching, launched or failed/not-launched state.
Cancel launch before multi-app completion closes the launcher, prevents further starts and preserves already-opened apps.
Dismiss before multi-app completion closes the launcher while remaining apps continue launching to completion.
Capture, close and relaunch an Edge/Chrome PWA installed in a non-default profile: same PWA/profile, not a generic browser or another profile.
For an elevation-capable packaged app, enable Launch as administrator, launch and approve UAC: elevated process/window is associated with the correct workspace entry.
A packaged app supporting command-line arguments applies the configured observable argument on launch.
Capture on monitor 1 only, connect monitor 2 and launch: every app remains on monitor 1 at the captured relative position.
Capture across two monitors, disconnect one and launch: every app recovers onto the remaining monitor; none remains off-screen.
Enabled Command Palette PowerToys extension Open Workspaces editor opens exactly one Workspaces Editor.
After creating a uniquely named workspace with two positioned apps and reopening Command Palette, the named result has correct app count/last-launched state and details list both apps.
Invoking that result launches the saved workspace with its persisted positions.
Under Windows Light, reopen Editor and Launcher: both follow the theme with readable Fluent controls, supported Mica/system backdrop and no legacy islands/unreadable text.
Under Windows Dark, reopen Editor and Launcher: both follow the theme with readable Fluent controls, supported Mica/system backdrop and no legacy islands/unreadable text.
Under Windows High Contrast, reopen Editor and Launcher: both follow the theme with readable Fluent controls, supported backdrop and no legacy islands/unreadable text.
